sentences.text: This intra-court appeal is filed under Section 4 of the Karnataka High Courts Act challenging the order dated 09.08.2021, passed in W.P.No.9791/2020 by the learned Single Judge.

2. Brief facts leading rise to filing of this appeal are as under:
The appellant claims to be the absolute owner of land bearing Sy.No.85/3 measuring 34 guntas situated at Kempanadodderi Village, Kora Hobli, Tumakuru Taluk and District under a registered sale deed dated 21.06.2016.

Respondent No.1 issued preliminary notification to acquire the entire extent of 34 guntas of land for installation of 220KV line by the KPTCL and for extension of the road without notifying the name of the appellant.
Respondent No.1 issued a final notification dated 04.10.2017, which was published in the local newspaper.
The petitioner filed a writ petition in W.P.No.9982/2018 challenging the acquisition proceedings.

This Court vide order dated 09.07.2019 disposed of the writ petition directing respondent Nos.2 and 3 that in case the petitioner submits a representation to the competent authority of respondent Nos.2 and 3, the competent authority shall deal with the same in accordance with law within two weeks and consider the representation.
Pursuant to the order of this Court in the aforesaid writ petition, the petitioner submitted a representation on 04.12.2019.

Respondent No.3 consider the representation submitted by the petitioner and rejected the representation of the appellant on Sri B K Ashok Kumar vs State Of Karnataka on 9 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116185692/

sentences.text: The petitioner aggrieved by the order passed by respondent No.3 by rejecting the representation of the appellant filed a writ petition in W.P.No.9791/2020.
The respondent No.3 filed the statement of objections contending that the land belonging to the appellant is required for widening of the road and also compacts of the industrial block.
The learned single Judge after hearing the parties dismissed the writ petition vide order dated 09.08.2021.
The appellant aggrieved by the order passed in the aforesaid writ petition, filed this writ appeal.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the Learned Additional Government Advocate for the respondents.
4.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the respondents have not conducted the joint measurement survey properly to ascertain as to who is in possession of the property and proceeded to issue final notification.
Respondent No.3 failed in performing his statutory duty in issuing a notice as required under Section 28(2) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966 (for short 'the Act').
Hence, on these grounds, the learned counsel for the appellant submits that the learned Single Judge has committed an error in dismissing the writ petition.
Hence, on these grounds, he prayed to allow the writ appeal.
5. Per contra, the learned Additional Government Advocate supports the impugned order.
6. The appellant purchased the land bearing Sy.No.85/3 measuring 34 guntas under a registered sale deed dated 21.06.2016.
Respondent No.1 issued a preliminary notification to acquire the entire extent of 34 guntas of land of the appellant for installation of 220KV line by the KPTCL and for extension of the road.
Though the appellant is the owner of said land, the respondent did not notify the name of the appellant in the preliminary notification.

The appellant filed the objections to the said acquisition proceedings contending that his name is not shown in the preliminary notification and no notice of acquisition has been issued to the appellant.

The appellant filed the writ petition in W.P.No.9982/2018 challenging the preliminary and final notification dated 23.03.2017 and 04.10.2017 respectively, insofar as the land of the appellant is concerned.

This court after hearing the parties, issued direction to the appellant to submit a representation to the competent authority i.e., respondent Nos.2 and 3 therein and the competent authority shall decide the same in accordance with law, within two weeks from the date of receipt of the such application.
Pursuant to the order passed by this Court in the aforesaid writ petition, the appellant has submitted a representation dated 04.12.2019 to the competent authority.

In the said representation it is contended that the appellant had purchased the property under a registered sale deed and also got converted the said land into non-agriculture and invested the huge amount for development and the land was not required for the public purpose.
Hence, prayed to drop the acquisition proceedings in respect of the appellant's land.
The competent authority considering the representation of the petitioner passed the order dated 23.07.2020 vide Annexure-N.

The competent authority has recorded a finding that the development officer has submitted a report stating that land of the appellant is required for the purpose of installation of 220KV line by the KPTCL for extension of road.
Hence, the request of the appellant for dropping the acquisition proceedings has been rejected.

sentences.text: From the perusal of the order passed by this Court in W.P.No.9982/2018, the appellant was aware about the issuance of preliminary and final notification and the appellant submitted a representation dated 04.12.2019 to the Special Land Acquisition Officer, KIADB.
The competent authority has already passed an order.

Thus, from the perusal of the records, it is clear that the land in question clearly falls within the larger industrial area, which is formed by acquiring the lands extending to more than four villagers.
Merely, the land of the appellant was converted into non-agricultural is not a ground to drop the acquisition proceedings.

7. In the case of SMT. RATHANMMA VS. STATE AND OTHERS, reported in 2016(1) KAR.LJ 558 held that the law permits acquisition of not only agricultural lands, but also lands converted into non-agricultural purpose, be it for residential purpose, commercial purpose, industrial purpose or any other purposes.

entities.text: SMT. RATHANMMA VS. STATE AND OTHERS
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The competent authority can initiate the acquisition proceedings not only in respect of agricultural land but also in respect of non-agricultural land.
If the non-agricultural land is acquired, then the compensation for a converted land would be entitled for higher compensation than an agricultural land.

The learned Singe Judge was of the opinion that there is no merit in the writ petition and accordingly, dismiss the writ petition.
8.
In view of the above discussion, we do not find any error in the impugned order.
Hence, we decline to interfere with the impugned order.

9. Accordingly, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The writ appeal is dismissed.
In view of disposal of the writ appeal, pending IAs., if any, do not survive for consideration and are accordingly disposed of.

Sd/-
